name: Petroglyphs of Lake Onega and the White Sea
description: In Russia's Republic of Karelia, roughly 4,500 carvings were pecked into bare shoreline rock some 6,000 to 7,000 years ago. Two groups, about 300 km apart, lie on Lake Onega and the White Sea. Onega's rocks show birds, animals, part-human creatures and sun or moon-like shapes, while the White Sea panels depict hunting, boats and footprints.
